keywords.name: Ability Pack
keywords.short_description: A pack of 3 random Abilities. Select 1 to install.
keywords.long_description:
An Ability Pack offers three random Abilities and lets you install one of them.
It is the Ability equivalent of a Part Pack or an Upgrade Pack, so the choice is between three options rather than a single fixed reward.
Because activating any Ability costs Energy, what you take is a question of what your Battery can sustain as much as what the Ability does.

keywords.name: Ability
keywords.short_description: Equippable tech that provides offensive, defensive, or utility capabilites. Consume Energy to activate.
keywords.long_description:
Abilities are equippable tech that give you offensive, defensive or utility options mid-race, and activating one consumes Energy.
Your Battery sets how much Energy you have to spend, Overcharged grants more of it temporarily and cuts reload times, and Disrupted blocks Abilities entirely.
Each one sits in a tree of its own, from Autopilot and Shield through Concussion Mine and Ion Blast, and upgrading it changes what it does rather than only how strong it is.

keywords.name: Afterburner
keywords.short_description: A safe and efficient boost. The tank gradually refills while racing.
keywords.long_description:
The Afterburner is the safe boost in Star Wars Galactic Racer: its tank gradually refills while you race, so using it costs you nothing but timing.
That is the difference between it and the Ramjet, which is more powerful but builds heat and can destroy the vehicle.
A takedown fully refills the tank, a perfect landing refills part or all of it through the Reconstituted Fuel parts, and the Fuel Injector upgrade track raises how much boost it gives.

keywords.name: Afterburner
keywords.short_description: How quickly the vehicle accelerates, decelerates, and how much boost is received from Afterburner.
keywords.long_description:
As a stat, Afterburner covers how quickly the vehicle accelerates and decelerates and how much boost the Afterburner itself delivers.
The Fuel Injector upgrade track is what raises it, which makes it the stat to invest in when corner exits are costing you time.
It is distinct from the Afterburner boost you fire on track, which has its own glossary entry and its own tank of fuel.

keywords.name: Air Brake
keywords.short_description: How tightly the vehicle can turn while Air Braking.
keywords.long_description:
Air Brake is how tightly a podracer can turn while air braking, and it is the Podracer class's advanced stat in Star Wars Galactic Racer.
Podracers are flown rather than driven, so the air brake is how they tighten a line instead of drifting or banking.
The Vector Servo upgrade track raises it, because the Advanced track always raises whatever a class calls its advanced stat.

keywords.name: Autopilot
keywords.short_description: Vehicle flies automatically for 10s. Ramjet heating reduced while active.
keywords.long_description:
Autopilot flies the vehicle automatically for 10 seconds and reduces Ramjet heating while it runs, which makes it the ability to reach for when the Ramjet needs to cool without giving up your line.
It is an ability rather than a status effect, so it has to be equipped and activated, and it ends when its timer does.
Its upgrades stretch that window and add a second effect: Surging Autopilot flies for 15 seconds and grants Surging, and Overcharged Autopilot flies for 20 seconds and grants Overcharged.
At the third tier, Overcharged Autopilot II adds 5 seconds each time you activate another ability, and Surging Autopilot II massively increases speed for the duration.

keywords.name: Battery
keywords.short_description: The maximum amount of Energy available to activate Abilities.
keywords.long_description:
Battery is the maximum Energy you have available to activate Abilities, so it sets how many you can use before you run dry.
The Power Cell upgrade track raises it, which is the investment that matters on any build leaning on Abilities rather than raw speed.
Energy itself is what gets spent, and Overcharged temporarily grants more of it while cutting reload times.

keywords.name: Braking
keywords.short_description: Decelerates vehicle.
keywords.long_description:
Braking decelerates the vehicle, and what it costs you depends entirely on the class you are driving.
A speeder bike turns braking into Kinetic Burst, which restores speed on release, while a podracer uses its Air Brake to tighten the line instead.
The Afterburner stat covers deceleration as well as acceleration, so the Fuel Injector upgrade track affects how the vehicle slows as well as how it picks up.

keywords.name: Burning
keywords.short_description: Causes Ramjet to rapidly gain heat.
keywords.long_description:
Burning makes the Ramjet gain heat rapidly, which shortens the window you have before it overheats and explodes.
It is applied by the Flame Vent ability, which cools the racer who fires it and leaves Burning and System Malfunction on everyone nearby, and by a number of parts that trade heat for power.
Cooled is the direct answer to it, so the Vent abilities and any part that grants Cooled will pull the heat back down, while the Afterfire and Heat Recycler traits turn the heat into something useful instead.

keywords.name: Chilled
keywords.short_description: Become Cooled, but gradually causes Frozen.
keywords.long_description:
Chilled grants Cooled, so the Ramjet recharges faster and heats more slowly, but it keeps building towards Frozen while it lasts.
That makes it a timed trade rather than a straight benefit in Star Wars Galactic Racer: the cooling is immediate and the steering penalty arrives if you sit in it too long.
Letting it run out clears it, and Shielded blocks it outright, since Shielded stops externally applied status effects from landing.

keywords.name: Choked
keywords.short_description: Disables Ramjet.
keywords.long_description:
Choked disables the Ramjet completely, so the boost you would normally lean on is simply unavailable until the effect clears.
It arrives from parts such as Choking Burn, and Corroded applies it as part of its own damage, which is what makes corrosion so dangerous.
Antacid Coating, Dechoking Mechanism and Particulate Filter are the parts built to resist or shorten it, and Shielded prevents it from being applied from outside in the first place.

keywords.name: Concussed
keywords.short_description: Causes impaired steering.
keywords.long_description:
Concussed impairs steering, so the vehicle answers the controls less precisely while it is on you.
The Concussion Mine and Concussive Bolt abilities exist to apply it: the mine drops a charge that detonates on proximity and leaves Concussed and System Malfunction on nearby opponents, while the bolt delivers it directly.
The Impact Regulator parts are the counter, and a Status Scrubber clears it along with any other negative effect and hands back a point of Energy for the trouble.

keywords.name: Concussion Mine
keywords.short_description: Drop a charge that explodes on proximity and applies Concussed and System Malfunction to nearby opponents.
keywords.long_description:
Concussion Mine drops a charge behind you that detonates on proximity, leaving Concussed and System Malfunction on any opponent close enough to catch it.
That pairing is what makes it dangerous: impaired steering from Concussed and heavy collision damage from System Malfunction arrive together.
It upgrades twice into Concussion Mine II and III, and Freezing Concussion Mine swaps the payload for Frozen. The Tooled Up and Trapper traits are built around laying them.

keywords.name: Cooled
keywords.short_description: Ramjet recharges more quickly and gains heat more slowly.
keywords.long_description:
Cooled makes the Ramjet recharge more quickly and gain heat more slowly, which is the effect every long Ramjet run in Star Wars Galactic Racer is built on.
The Vent family of abilities grants it, from plain Vent through Auto-Vent, Cooling Blast and Supercooled Vent, and dozens of parts hand it out on a trigger such as a perfect landing or a takedown.
It is the counter to Burning and to Redlining, and the Ramjet Rider racer style is the one that commits to it, extending the Ramjet as long as possible rather than pushing it to the limit.

keywords.name: Cornering
keywords.short_description: How quickly and tightly the vehicle can take corners.
keywords.long_description:
Cornering is how quickly and tightly the vehicle takes corners, and the Repulsor Grip upgrade track is what raises it.
The Insulated Servos parts protect it, while Exposed Servos is the faulty counterpart that gives it away.
It sits alongside each class's own cornering technique, whether that is Drift, Knife Edge, Kinetic Burst or the podracer's Air Brake.

keywords.name: Corroded
keywords.short_description: Chokes Ramjet, causing it to disable. Continued exposure quickly leads to Crash.
keywords.long_description:
Corroded chokes the Ramjet so it disables, and continued exposure leads quickly to a Crash, which makes it the most punishing status effect in the game.
The Corrosive Vent ability applies it, and so do parts like Acid Battery and Acidic Fuel, which accept corrosion as the price of their own bonus.
Corrode Resistance makes it take 200% longer to reach a Crash, Antacid Coating and Chassis Cleansing work against it directly, and Acrid Alarm warns you while it is running.

keywords.name: Crash Ability
keywords.short_description: Activated during a Crash. Does not cost Energy.
keywords.long_description:
A Crash Ability is one you activate during a Crash, and it costs no Energy to use.
Four abilities work this way in Star Wars Galactic Racer: Charging Blast, Cooling Blast, Ion Blast and Shielding Blast.
Each one turns the crash into something, whether that is Overcharged, Cooled, Disrupted on nearby opponents or Shielded for the recovery.

keywords.name: Crash
keywords.short_description: Catastrophic vehicle failure due to collision, impact, or explosion. Limited Crashes allowed per event.
keywords.long_description:
A Crash is catastrophic vehicle failure from a collision, an impact or an explosion, and each event allows only a limited number of them.
Corroded is the status effect most likely to cause one, since continued exposure leads quickly to a Crash, and Corrode Resistance buys 200% longer before that happens.
The Crash Abilities are activated during one and cost no Energy, and the Bounce Back, Mint Condition and One More Chance traits are all about surviving or recovering from them.

keywords.name: Critical Malfunction
keywords.short_description: Causes high susceptibility to collision damage. Afterburner, Ramjet, and Abilities are disabled.
keywords.long_description:
A Critical Malfunction leaves the vehicle highly susceptible to collision damage and shuts down the Afterburner, the Ramjet and your Abilities at the same time.
It is the worst of the malfunction states, and recovering from it is the whole point of parts like Critical Assist and Systematic Servicing and of the Accelerated Recovery trait.
Critical Injectors turn the moment into speed instead, and the Resilience upgrade track is what makes malfunctions less likely to land at all.

keywords.name: Disrupted
keywords.short_description: Blocks Abilities and Overcharged while applying Choked, System Malfunction, and reducing speed.
keywords.long_description:
Disrupted is the shutdown effect: it blocks Abilities and Overcharged, applies Choked and System Malfunction, and reduces your speed while it holds.
The Ion Bolt ability locks on to the nearest opponent to apply it, and the Blast abilities, Concussive Bolt and their upgrades all carry it as well.
Disruption Protection is the part that resists it, Shielded blocks it from landing, and a Status Scrubber clears it once it is on you.

keywords.name: Drift
keywords.short_description: How sharply the landspeeder turns and how much speed is maintained while using Drift.
keywords.long_description:
Drift is how sharply a landspeeder turns and how much speed it keeps while drifting, and it is the Landspeeder class's advanced stat.
Landspeeders hold a line by breaking traction deliberately, which is what separates them from the skim speeder's Knife Edge and the bike's Kinetic Burst.
The Vector Servo upgrade track raises it, since the Advanced track follows whichever technique the class is built around.

keywords.name: Energy
keywords.short_description: Spent to activate Abilities. Increased by Battery.
keywords.long_description:
Energy is spent to activate Abilities, and your Battery stat sets how much of it you can hold.
Parts like Kinetic Energizer and Fuel Synthesis generate it during a race, and a Status Scrubber hands a point back whenever it actually clears something.
Overcharged grants temporary Energy on top of your Battery and reduces reload times, while Disrupted blocks Abilities entirely, so the Energy simply sits there.

keywords.name: Fault
keywords.short_description: A malfunctioning Part that cannot be replaced until repaired. Faults can be repaired at the Scrap Dealer.
keywords.long_description:
A fault is a damaged part that keeps its slot on the vehicle and works against you until it is repaired, and 66 of the parts in Star Wars Galactic Racer are faults rather than upgrades.
Each one carries a penalty in place of a bonus: Faulty Abilities makes abilities reload 300% slower, and Cracked Battery leaves you Corroded every time you activate one.
A faulty part cannot be replaced while it is still broken, so clearing one means taking the vehicle to the Scrap Dealer, where every repair is bought.

keywords.name: Flame Vent
keywords.short_description: Gain Cooled and reduce Ramjet heat. Applies Burning and System Malfunction to nearby opponents.
keywords.long_description:
Flame Vent cools your own Ramjet while leaving Burning and System Malfunction on every opponent nearby.
It is the aggressive member of the Vent family: the heat you shed goes onto everyone around you rather than simply disappearing.
The Firestarter trait builds on it, and an opponent carrying Shielded will not take the Burning at all, since Shielded blocks externally applied effects.

keywords.name: Frozen
keywords.short_description: Significantly impairs steering, as well as cools Ramjet.
keywords.long_description:
Frozen significantly impairs steering but it also cools the Ramjet, so it is both a penalty and a cooling effect depending on what you were trying to do.
Freezing Concussion Mine and Supercooled Vent apply it, the latter deliberately: it cools hard and disengages once you are fully Frozen.
Freeze Resistance and Endothermic Repulsors reduce what it costs you, while the Absolute Zero, Permafrost and Null Heat Signature traits build on it instead of avoiding it.

keywords.name: Ion Bolt
keywords.short_description: Lock on to the closest nearby opponent and apply Disrupted to target.
keywords.long_description:
Ion Bolt locks on to the closest nearby opponent and applies Disrupted to them.
That single hit blocks their Abilities and Overcharged, applies Choked and System Malfunction and reduces their speed, which is why it is the strongest interference tool in the game.
The Prepared trait supports it, and a target already carrying Shielded is immune to the effect.

keywords.name: Kinetic Burst
keywords.short_description: How powerful the speeder bike's Kinetic Burst braking is and how much speed is restored upon release.
keywords.long_description:
Kinetic Burst is how powerful a speeder bike's braking is and how much speed it restores when you release it, and it is the Speeder Bike class's advanced stat.
The bike slows hard and then gives the speed back, which is how a class that runs wide in corners still carries pace through them.
The Vector Servo upgrade track raises it, as it does every class's advanced stat.

keywords.name: Knife Edge
keywords.short_description: How tightly the skim speeder turns and how much speed is maintained while using Knife Edge.
keywords.long_description:
Knife Edge is the Skim Speeder's advanced stat in Star Wars Galactic Racer: roll the speeder onto its edge with the steering input and it corners far more tightly while holding on to more of its speed.
It is a technique rather than a status effect, so nothing applies or removes it. You hold it through the corner and come off it on the exit.
The Vector Servo upgrade track is what raises it, because the Advanced track always raises whatever a class calls its advanced stat, and on a skim speeder that is Knife Edge.
It works alongside the class traits it ships with, Streamlined Intakes for top speed on smooth wide lines and Sweeping Airfoils for graceful banked cornering.

keywords.name: Maneuvering
keywords.short_description: Use Improved Steering to Drift, Kinetic Burst, or Knife Edge.
keywords.long_description:
Maneuvering is the stat behind Improved Steering, which is what you use to Drift, to hold a Knife Edge or to fire a Kinetic Burst.
Each class has its own technique bound to it, so what the stat does for you depends on what you are driving.
The Afterburnout trait builds on it, and the Vector Servo upgrade track raises whichever advanced technique your class uses.

keywords.name: Overcharged
keywords.short_description: Gain temporary Energy and reduce Ability reload times.
keywords.long_description:
Overcharged grants temporary Energy and cuts Ability reload times, so it is the window in which you can chain Abilities far faster than normal.
Charging Blast grants it during a Crash, and the Overcharged Autopilot abilities grant it for the 20 seconds they fly the vehicle for you.
Parts such as Charging Coils and Overcharged Injector extend or exploit it, and Disrupted is what takes it away, since it blocks Overcharged outright.

keywords.name: Overtaking Surge
keywords.short_description: Gain Surging for 10s, lost on impact. Overtakes extend the duration and increase its potency.
keywords.long_description:
Overtaking Surge grants Surging for 10 seconds, and every overtake while it runs extends the duration and increases its potency.
Like plain Surge it is lost on impact, so it rewards passing cleanly rather than fighting through traffic.
The Overtaker trait is built around it, and it is the ability of choice when there is a field in front of you rather than clear air.

keywords.name: Part Pack
keywords.short_description: A pack of 3 random Parts. Select 1 to install.
keywords.long_description:
A Part Pack offers three random Parts and lets you install one of them.
Rarity decides how strong the effect is, so a pack is usually a choice between a strong effect you cannot build around and a weaker one you can.
The Parts themselves are passive, so what you install here changes how the vehicle behaves for the rest of the run rather than giving you something to activate.

keywords.name: Part
keywords.short_description: Installed to a vehicle to provide passive effects. The higher the rarity, the stronger the effect.
keywords.long_description:
A Part is installed to a vehicle to give it a passive effect, and the higher its rarity the stronger that effect is.
Parts run from Common through Rare, Epic and Legendary, with Experimental as its own case and Faulty as the opposite: a fault keeps its slot and works against you until it is repaired.
They are what tie the rest of the glossary together, since most parts trigger off a status effect, a landing, a takedown or the Ramjet heat you are carrying.

keywords.name: Perfect Landing
keywords.short_description: Landing a jump with vehicle pitch parallel to the ground results in a temporary boost.
keywords.long_description:
A perfect landing in Star Wars Galactic Racer is a jump you touch down from with the vehicle level, pitched parallel to the ground, and it pays out as a temporary boost.
Nothing applies it but your own landing angle, so it rewards flattening out in the air instead of nosing in, and it is gone as soon as the boost runs out.
Several parts build on it: Reconstituted Fuel refills the Afterburner tank by half or completely, and Cooling Dampers grants Cooled for 5 or 10 seconds on a perfect landing.
Two traits go further, with Repulsor Fuel Link filling the tank and doubling the power of its next use, and Repulsor Alignment counting every one of your landings as perfect.

keywords.name: Perfect Start
keywords.short_description: Temporary boost gained from Perfect acceleration check upon race start.
keywords.long_description:
A Perfect Start is the temporary boost you get for passing the acceleration check as the race begins.
It is one of the Pre-Race Checks, so it is decided before the first corner rather than earned on track.
The Optimized Inlets parts widen the window for it, Charging Coils turn it into Overcharged, and Faulty Activator and Imprecise Calibration are the faults that cost you it.

keywords.name: Pre-Race Checks
keywords.short_description: Checks at race start which, when completed successfully, give additional benefits.
keywords.long_description:
Pre-Race Checks are the checks that run as a race starts, and completing them successfully gives you additional benefits.
The Perfect Start is the one most builds care about, since passing the acceleration check converts straight into a temporary boost.
Parts that key off the start, such as Defensive Start and Unsettled Start, decide what those first seconds are worth to you.

keywords.name: Ramjet
keywords.short_description: How much boost is provided by the Ramjet.
keywords.long_description:
As a stat, Ramjet is how much boost the Ramjet delivers when you use it, and the Turbojet Manifold upgrade track is what raises it.
Raising it makes each Ramjet run worth more without changing how quickly the heat builds, which is handled by Cooled, Burning and the cooling parts.
The boost itself, the heat it generates and the explosion that follows overheating have their own glossary entry.

keywords.name: Ramjet
keywords.short_description: A powerful but dangerous boost. Managing the heat it generates will prevent exploding.
keywords.long_description:
The Ramjet is the powerful boost in Star Wars Galactic Racer and the one that can end a race: holding it builds heat, and letting that heat run away makes the vehicle explode.
The Turbojet Manifold upgrade track raises the Ramjet stat, and the status effects around it decide how long you can lean on it.
Cooled makes the Ramjet recharge faster and gain heat more slowly, while Burning makes it gain heat rapidly, Choked disables it outright, and Corroded chokes it on the way to a crash. Chilled and Frozen both cool it at the cost of steering.
That trade is what the Redliner, Firebug and Ramjet Rider racer styles are built around, from pushing the Ramjet to its limit to extending it as long as possible.

keywords.name: Redlining
keywords.short_description: Racing within the red zone prior to the Ramjet overheating and exploding, indicated by an alarm.
keywords.long_description:
Redlining is racing in the red zone before the Ramjet overheats and explodes, and an alarm tells you when you are in it.
It is the most rewarded risk in the game: the Extended Alarm parts widen the window, Early Warning tells you sooner, and Critical Ramjet Power pays out for staying in it.
Auto-Vent is the ability that reacts to it by cooling automatically, while Defective Alarm is the faulty part that takes the warning away.

keywords.name: Resilience
keywords.short_description: How well the vehicle can handle damage, avoid Malfunctions, and resist negative status effects.
keywords.long_description:
Resilience is how well the vehicle handles damage, avoids Malfunctions and resists negative status effects.
The Structural Bracing upgrade track raises it, which makes it the defensive stat on any build that expects contact.
It is what stands between you and a System Malfunction or a Critical Malfunction, and it works alongside Shielded rather than replacing it.

keywords.name: Shield
keywords.short_description: Gain Shielded for 10s.
keywords.long_description:
Shield grants Shielded for 10 seconds, raising protection from collisions and impacts and blocking status effects applied from outside.
It is the pre-emptive defence rather than a repair: used before contact it stops the damage and the status, used after it does neither.
The Protected trait extends what it gives you, and Shielding Blast is the version you can use during a Crash for no Energy.

keywords.name: Shielded
keywords.short_description: Increases protection from collisions and impacts as well as blocks externally-applied status effects.
keywords.long_description:
Shielded increases protection from collisions and impacts and blocks externally applied status effects, which makes it the defensive effect in Star Wars Galactic Racer.
The Shield ability grants it for 10 seconds, and Impact Shield, Shielding Blast and Surging Shield all carry their own version of it.
It is the pre-emptive answer to anything an opponent can throw at you, from Concussed to Choked, and parts like Inertial Shield and Defensive Start decide when you get it.

keywords.name: Shockwave
keywords.short_description: Blast nearby opponents away and apply System Malfunction to affected opponents.
keywords.long_description:
Shockwave blasts nearby opponents away from you and leaves System Malfunction on everyone it catches.
The push is the point: it clears the space around you and leaves the field far more vulnerable to the next contact.
Vectored Shockwave is the directed version, which propels you forward as it fires, and the Tooled Up trait supports both.

keywords.name: Slipstreaming
keywords.short_description: A speed bonus gained while flying closely behind an opponent.
keywords.long_description:
Slipstreaming is the speed bonus you gain while flying closely behind an opponent, so it only exists when there is traffic in front of you.
The Improved Drafting and Stronger Slipstreaming parts and the Airflow Alignment and Optimized Profile traits all deepen it, and Cooling Slipstream turns the tow into Cooled.
The Slipstreamer racer style is built around it, and Inefficient Aerodynamics is the faulty part that takes it away.

keywords.name: Speed
keywords.short_description: The unboosted top speed of your vehicle.
keywords.long_description:
Speed is the unboosted top speed of your vehicle, which is the figure everything else is measured against.
Every upgrade track raises it as well as its own stat, so top speed climbs no matter which track you invest in.
Surging and the two boosts, Afterburner and Ramjet, all push you past it temporarily, while Disrupted and Frozen take it away.

keywords.name: Status Scrubber
keywords.short_description: Clear negative status effects. If any are cleared, recover 1 Energy.
keywords.long_description:
Status Scrubber clears negative status effects, and if it actually cleared something it hands back a point of Energy.
It is the answer to the effects you cannot otherwise shake, from Concussed and Choked to Disrupted and Corroded.
Auto-Scrubber and Multi-Scrubber are the upgraded versions, and the Careful trait builds on cleaning yourself up.

keywords.name: Supercooled Vent
keywords.short_description: Gain Cooled and reduce Ramjet heat while gradually gaining Frozen. Upon fully Frozen, Vent disengages.
keywords.long_description:
Supercooled Vent grants Cooled and sheds Ramjet heat while gradually making you Frozen, and it disengages the moment you are fully Frozen.
It is the strongest cooling in the game and it ends on a timer you cannot extend, because the Frozen build-up is what shuts it off.
Frozen significantly impairs steering, so the cooling is bought with precision, and the Supercooled trait is the one built around that trade.

keywords.name: Surge
keywords.short_description: Gain Surging for 10s, lost on impact. Overtakes extend the duration.
keywords.long_description:
Surge is the ability that grants Surging for 10 seconds, raising acceleration and speed for the duration.
The effect is lost on impact, so it rewards clean air, and every overtake you make while it runs extends how long it lasts.
The Extra Fuel trait builds on it, and Overtaking Surge is the upgraded version that leans entirely on passing traffic to keep it alive.

keywords.name: Surging
keywords.short_description: Increases acceleration and speed.
keywords.long_description:
Surging increases acceleration and speed, and it is the most widely supported positive effect in the game.
The Surge ability grants it for 10 seconds and loses it on impact, Overtaking Surge extends the duration each time you pass someone, and Impact Surge turns contact into speed instead of losing it.
Dozens of parts grant it on a trigger, and the Combat Adrenaline, In the Zone and Power to Thrusters traits tie it to fighting, position or shielding.

keywords.name: System Malfunction
keywords.short_description: Causes high susceptibility to collision damage.
keywords.long_description:
System Malfunction leaves the vehicle highly susceptible to collision damage, so the next contact hurts far more than it otherwise would.
It is what most of the offensive kit applies: Concussion Mines, Flame Vent, the Shockwave abilities and Disrupted all leave it behind.
Emergency Cooling and Failsafe Coolant soften it, the Good As New and Accelerated Recovery traits shorten it, and Afterburner Reconfiguration makes the Afterburner 100% more powerful while it is on you.

keywords.name: Takedown
keywords.short_description: Any action directly causing an opponent to Crash. Fully refills Afterburner tank.
keywords.long_description:
A Takedown is any action that directly causes an opponent to Crash, and it fully refills your Afterburner tank as a reward.
That refill is why aggression pays in Star Wars Galactic Racer: the boost you spend getting alongside someone comes straight back if they go out.
Impact Surge turns the contact into Surging, the Cooling Actuator parts turn it into Cooled, and the Combat Adrenaline and Energy Hunter traits pay out on it too.

keywords.name: Upgrade Pack
keywords.short_description: A pack of 3 random +1 Upgrades. Select 1 to install.
keywords.long_description:
An Upgrade Pack offers three random +1 Upgrades and lets you install one of them.
Every one of them raises top speed as well as its own stat, so there is no wrong pick, only a question of which stat you want the extra point in.
The six stats they draw from are Afterburner, Battery, Cornering, Maneuvering, Ramjet and Resilience.

keywords.name: Upgrade
keywords.short_description: Upgrades the vehicle’s top speed and one of its stats: Afterburner, Battery, Cornering, Maneuvering, Ramjet, or Resilience.
keywords.long_description:
An Upgrade raises your vehicle's top speed and one of its stats: Afterburner, Battery, Cornering, Maneuvering, Ramjet or Resilience.
That is why top speed climbs whichever track you invest in, and why the six tracks are a question of what you want on top of the speed.
Each track has its own name on the vehicle, from Fuel Injector and Power Cell to Repulsor Grip, Vector Servo, Turbojet Manifold and Structural Bracing.

keywords.name: Vectored Shockwave
keywords.short_description: Blast nearby opponents away, propelling you forward and applying System Malfunction to affected opponents.
keywords.long_description:
Vectored Shockwave blasts nearby opponents away and propels you forward as it fires, applying System Malfunction to anyone it catches.
That forward push is what separates it from the plain Shockwave, which clears space without moving you.
The Center of Attention trait is built around it, rewarding having traffic close enough to be worth hitting.

keywords.name: Vent
keywords.short_description: Gain Cooled and reduce Ramjet heat.
keywords.long_description:
Vent grants Cooled and reduces Ramjet heat, which is the basic cooling ability in Star Wars Galactic Racer.
It is what lets you hold the Ramjet longer than its heat alone would allow, and the Exhaust trait builds on it.
The family extends from here: Auto-Vent reacts to Redlining, Flame Vent passes the heat to your rivals, Corrosive Vent corrodes them, and Supercooled Vent cools hardest of all.

styles.name: Afterburner
styles.description: A straightforward style that relies on the power of Afterburner rather than the Ramjet.

styles.name: Brawler
styles.description: An aggressive style that rewards battling and Takedowns.

styles.name: BT310 Quadra
styles.description: BT310 QUADRA: Named for its four engines, the BT310 Quadra was originally a factory-built rental. Ben Quadinaros refitted the vehicle with new power couplings and custom systems, taming the powerful, but temperamental podracer.

styles.name: Clean Racer
styles.description: A deft style that rewards non-combative racing.

styles.name: Custom Ord Pedrovia
styles.description: CUSTOM ORD PEDROVIA: Built from scratch to suit Gasgano’s needs, his custom Ord Pedrovia podracer features a bespoke Afterburner tank, easily leaving competitors in the dust. Though this strength comes at the cost of increased drag, it’s no matter to Gasgano, who’s already pulled into the lead.

styles.name: Engineer
styles.description: A strategic style that benefits from clearing negative status effects.

styles.name: Exelbrok XL 5115
styles.description: EXELBROK XL 5115: Speed is no challenge for the Exelbrok XL 5115, thanks to cycles of work done by Ody’s loyal pit droid team on the podracer's immense twin engines. Even with its reduced cornering, the vehicle is a marvel waiting to be challenged.

styles.name: Firebug
styles.description: A potent style built for bursts of extreme speed with a short but powerful Ramjet.

styles.name: Ice Cold
styles.description: An advanced style for racers eager to take advantage of Frozen.

styles.name: IPG-X1131 LongTail
styles.description: IPG-X1131 LONGTAIL: Teemto Pagalies’ IPG-X1131 LongTail features a unique circular shape. The internal cycling ring functions as a gyroscopic stabilizer, allowing it to keep up with more aerodynamic podracers. But what improvements the cycling ring grants in cornering, it sacrifices in speed.

styles.name: Plug-F Mammoth
styles.description: PLUG-F MAMMOTH: The legendary Sebulba’s Plug-F Mammoth is an icon as well as a brute, boasting a robust exterior designed to take down opponents while preserving its own integrity. That isn’t to mention the removable systems built for bending former track regulations, such as flame vents.

styles.name: Ramjet Rider
styles.description: A controlled style for those looking to extend Ramjet as long as possible.

styles.name: Redliner
styles.description: A high-risk style for those who dare to push their Ramjet to the limit.

styles.name: Slipstreamer
styles.description: A smooth style for using opponents' slipstreams to overtake them.

styles.name: Stunt Runner
styles.description: A performative style that takes advantage of jumps to surprise opponents and extend Afterburner.

styles.name: Survivor
styles.description: A defensive style for those who want to race without interference.

styles.name: Tech Expert
styles.description: A technical style for racers who want to take full advantage of Abilities.

styles.name: Tenacious
styles.description: A steadfast style that improves performance in risky situations.

styles.name: Vulptereen 327
styles.description: VULPTEREEN 327: Built on his homeworld of Vulpter, the Vulptereen 327 podracer is perfect for the aggressive Dud Bolt, boasting excellent traction to power down straights. A vehicle built tough, Dud Bolt's favorite pastime is ramming into his opponents as he flies by unscathed, laughing as he does.

styles.name: Weaponized
styles.description: A deadly style for those interested in playing offense.

racers.name: Ary Quill
racers.description: Hailing from a long line of racing champions, audacious Ary Quill will stop at nothing to prove she’s worthy of carrying on the Quill family legacy. Being deceived by Kestar Bool has only sharpened the Namaran's ambitions…
racers.summary: Ary Quill races the NL-4 Landspeeder with the Redliner style. They are unlocked by: Reach Multiplayer Rank 5. They race in the Multiplayer Tour.

racers.name: Ben Quadinaros
racers.description: Ben Quadinaros’ debut in the big leagues made him a mockery when his vehicle failed at the race start. But the Toong didn’t let that stop him, and soon he was considered the legendary Sebulba’s greatest podracing rival.
racers.summary: Ben Quadinaros races Ben Quadinaros's Podracer with the Afterburner style. They race in the Podracing Tour.

racers.name: Biddy Blas
racers.description: Biddy Blas was promised fame and fortune in exchange for racing under Kestar Bool’s banner. After Huttball, modelling, and jatz failed to give the hot-headed Crocin the limelight he craved, the Galactic League is his last shot at getting his face on a cereal box, just like his mama always dreamed.
racers.summary: Biddy Blas races the Pel'ake Speeder Bike with the Firebug style. They are unlocked by: Reach Multiplayer Rank 25. They race in the Multiplayer Tour.

racers.name: Dud Bolt
racers.description: Dud Bolt holds no shame in doing whatever it takes to win…or earn a paycheck. The Vulptereen is a fan favorite on the track, as well as an ally of Sebulba’s, who has on many occasions paid the racer to take down fellow competitors mid-race.
racers.summary: Dud Bolt races Dud Bolt's Podracer with the Afterburner style. They race in the Podracing Tour.

racers.name: Fola Kanjen
racers.description: Racing on the backs of local farmers’ cattle could only ever get Fola Kanjen so far. In the Galactic League, she races as fast as her thrill-seeking heart desires—and she doesn’t have to listen when someone tells her no.
racers.summary: Fola Kanjen races the Rathtar Skim Speeder with the Tenacious style. They are unlocked by: Reach Multiplayer Rank 21. They race in the Multiplayer Tour.

racers.name: Gasgano
racers.description: Unwilling to back down despite ruthless competitors, Gasgano leaves nothing behind on the track. With his four arms, he makes podracing look easy, earning the Xexto celebrity status.
racers.summary: Gasgano races Gasgano's Podracer with the Afterburner style. They race in the Podracing Tour.

racers.name: Goli & 02-R0
racers.description: A prodigious racing talent far from their home of Polis Massa for the first time, the meek but kind-hearted Goli, alongside companion droid 02-R0, is eager to find a place amongst the League’s boisterous racers.
racers.summary: Goli & 02-R0 races the SU-3 Skim Speeder with the Clean Racer style. They are unlocked by: Reach Multiplayer Rank 17. They race in the Multiplayer Tour.

racers.name: Griff Halloran
racers.description: Still sporting the armor from his days flying in the Imperial Navy, Griff Halloran struggles to fit into the changing galaxy. Flying is the one thing he knows he's good at—and the one thing he'll fight to keep.
racers.summary: Griff Halloran races the Ta'han Skim Speeder with the Afterburner style. They are unlocked by: Reach Multiplayer Rank 3. They race in the Multiplayer Tour.

racers.name: Hibi
racers.description: An energetic gearhead with a prodigious talent for inventing wonders (as well as blowing them up), charismatic Hibi has recently paid her dues serving as Shade’s ship mechanic. But in the Galactic League, the Ardennian can finally make her mark as one of the galaxy’s great engineers.

racers.name: Katja Mox
racers.description: With her family’s shipping empire, the Imperial-loyal MoxCorp, disbanded by the New Republic, the unflappable Katja Mox reawakens the racing passion of her youth to forge her own destiny apart from her disgraced family name.
racers.summary: Katja Mox races the Kreed Speeder Bike with the Tech Expert style. They are unlocked by: Reach Multiplayer Rank 1. They race in the Multiplayer Tour.

racers.name: Kestar Bool
racers.description: Fans, racers, and legends all cheering his name… Kestar Bool wouldn’t have it any other way. The proud, underhanded son of the tyrannical Bool family will do whatever it takes to retain his place as Galactic League Champion and earn the respect he believes he deserves—from the public as well as his iron-willed father.
racers.summary: Kestar Bool races Kestar Bool's Podracer with the Weaponized style. They are unlocked by: Reach Multiplayer Rank 39.

racers.name: Lyren Shok
racers.description: Fame, adoration, and fans with short memories are all Lyren Shok needs—especially after an…unfortunate…scandal waylaid the Nautolan's career as a celebrity waveskimmer racer. The Galactic League offers a new start and a new fanbase, and being buddies with Kestar Bool doesn't hurt.
racers.summary: Lyren Shok races the Wist L Skim Speeder with the Stunt Runner style. They are unlocked by: Reach Multiplayer Rank 33. They race in the Multiplayer Tour.

racers.name: Malis Vazosk
racers.description: For Malis, racing and mercenary work are one and the same: there’s violence, and there’s the compensation for it. These days, it’s the Bools who line the brutal Trandoshan’s pockets.
racers.summary: Malis Vazosk races the Zillo Speeder Bike with the Brawler style. They are unlocked by: Reach Multiplayer Rank 29. They race in the Multiplayer Tour.

racers.name: Nik Skandaro
racers.description: No one understands the ruthless Bools better than their former enforcer. Now in his sunset years, the gruff and imposing Zabrak scorns Kestar’s domineering presence on the League, wanting nothing more than to find some solace racing his beloved speeders.
racers.summary: Nik Skandaro races the Jakobeast Landspeeder with the Survivor style. They are unlocked by: Reach Multiplayer Rank 11. They race in the Multiplayer Tour.

racers.name: Ody Mandrell
racers.description: Growing up on Tatooine meant Ody Mandrell was only a child when he first dreamed of making his mark on the podracing tracks. The Er’Kit did so, setting records with his pit droid team that forced fans and racers to remember his name.
racers.summary: Ody Mandrell races Ody Mandrell's Podracer with the Afterburner style. They race in the Podracing Tour.

racers.name: Sebulba
racers.description: Sebulba carved out a well-deserved place in history as one of the galaxy’s greatest racers. As canny as ever despite his advancing years, he's insisted on finding a role for himself in the Galactic League, unwilling to allow his legendary name to be forgotten.
racers.summary: Sebulba races Sebulba's Podracer with the Brawler style. They race in the Podracing Tour.

racers.name: Sen Fira
racers.description: Sen Fira would sooner put a blaster to Kestar Bool’s skull than bow down to him, but the debt she owes the Bools forces her to bend the knee. The unshaken Tognath races for Kestar in the hopes that one day the debt will be repaid and she can reunite with her eggmate.
racers.summary: Sen Fira races the Revasi G Speeder Bike with the Slipstreamer style. They are unlocked by: Reach Multiplayer Rank 23. They race in the Multiplayer Tour.

racers.name: Shade
racers.description: Dauntless cargo pilot Shade once dreamt of the race track, but growing up on Gathleon under the oppressive Bool conglomerate left the dream a fantasy. Darius Pax’s Galactic League offers Shade a new start. There, Shade can pursue that childhood dream. There, Shade can take down Kestar Bool, the arrogant scion who made Shade’s life hell. Racing is sweet, but justice is sweeter.
racers.summary: Shade races the ARZ 41 Landspeeder with the Ramjet Rider style. They race in the Multiplayer Tour.

racers.name: Soren Zaks
racers.description: As a boy, Soren Zaks dreamed of nothing more than becoming the best racer in the galaxy. But after years of compromise as a desperate and destitute underworld smuggler, good-hearted Soren seeks to reshape and redeem his life by returning to the racetrack.
racers.summary: Soren Zaks races the KJC 99 Landspeeder with the Engineer style. They are unlocked by: Reach Multiplayer Rank 7. They race in the Multiplayer Tour.

racers.name: Teemto Pagalies
racers.description: The charming Teemto Pagalies is popular everywhere except his own homeworld, from which he was outcast. The Veknoid doesn’t complain. He’s got all the fans he needs cheering for him on the track.
racers.summary: Teemto Pagalies races Teemto Pagalies's Podracer with the Afterburner style. They race in the Podracing Tour.

_doc.about: Hand-curated semantics per part family (non-fault parts). Vocabulary is shared with racer-style/ability/trait tagging so the planner can match sources to consumers.
_doc.needs: Conditions the part is useless without. Statuses (Cooled, Frozen, Surging, Shielded, Overcharged, Burning, Corroded, Concussed, SysMalf, CritMalf) need a source. Mechanics (Takedown, PerfectLanding, PerfectStart, Airborne, Slipstreaming, Redlining, Crash, LastCrash, Ramjet, Afterburner, Ability, Energy, Speed, FirstPlace, RaceStart, Collision) depend on playstyle/track.
_doc.grants: Statuses the part produces (makes it a source for other consumers).
_doc.boosts: What improves: Ramjet, Afterburner, Speed, Cornering, Abilities, Energy, Cooled (potency), Surging (potency), Slipstreaming, Crash (extra life), Redlining (zone), Ramjet-heat (less heat / faster cooling).

_doc.about: What each racer style is built around, in the same vocabulary as part_semantics.json. 'core' = the mechanic the style's traits reward (the planner treats it as the primary scoring axis). 'grants' = statuses the style itself supplies via traits or its multiplayer starting ability, so consumer parts for them are 'free'. 'mechanics' = play patterns the style pushes you into (so parts triggered by them fire often). Derived from racer_style_traits + racer_style_abilities; adjust by hand as needed.
_doc.modes: Campaign styles have rank 1-3 trait sets; multiplayer has a fixed set plus a starting ability. The planner reads traits per mode from the DB; this file only adds the interpretation.
